newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's trade surplus for August.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's trade surplus for August.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' reactions to Japan's trade surplus for August, which dropped 31 percent from a year earlier to 369.47 billion yen.
The surplus came in slightly above expectations. A Reuter poll of analysts had shown that the surplus would be between 160 billion and 314 billion yen in August.
SUSUMU KATO, CHIEF ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL

"You've seen some recovery in export volume due to the depreciation of the yen, which made Japanese exporters recover competitiveness, such as in autos, shipbuilding...I think there is a recovery in export activity in Japan."

"Japan's oil imports were up almost 15 percent year-on-year, so the recent increase in oil prices increased overall import value in Japan. So Japan now has large deficit with oil exporting countries."
NOBUYUKI SAJI, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT NIKKO RESEARCH CENTER
"The yen's weakness against the dollar has begun to restrict the pace of increase of import volume. Some importers may lose their competitiveness at an exchange rate of 105-110 yen."

"Also we're hoping for a recovery in consumption on the back of improving labour market conditions. This should also fuel demand for foreign goods, particularly U.S.-made autos, for example. And as a result we do expect the trade surplus to continue to drop quite rapidly even in the second half of this year...We think it is going to fall faster. We are looking at a 50 percent year-on-year decline.

"...upward potential for a strong rebound in exports is relatively limited. We're poised for further import growth later this year. Given this backdrop, I think we can look for further decline at a very rapid pace of the trade surplus."
